title: Outcome diary — weekly retrospective & micro-OKRs (personal)
content:
Quick log — weekly outcome diary (personal)

Context: quick, messy scratchpad for tracking a handful of personal outcome experiments and micro-OKRs tied to the dev-experience work. Not shared as a polished update; used to surface decisions for 1:1 and weekly syncs.

Snapshot metrics (week Feb 22–28) — leading indicators I care about:
- Time spent heads-down (code + debugging): 9.5h (goal 12h)
- PRs opened: 4; PRs merged: 3 (2 after reviewer follow-ups)
- Avg PR review turnaround: 24h (target < 12h) — regressions on Wed (context below)
- Onboarding test: new hire sandbox completed end-to-end: 55% (manual steps left)
- Personal micro-OKR progress: 45% toward Q1 ambition (reduce latency of dev loop + improve onboarding flow)

What I shipped / experiment notes:
1) Local KV-cache warmup script (prototype)
   - Goal: reduce first-token latency for cold-start customer workloads by pre-warming KV entries for common prefixes.
   - Notes: used small script that replays top-20 prefixes from telemetry for 60s during instance boot. Saw median first-token time drop ~18% in my local perf harness.
   - Risks: increases memory use and slightly longer boot — safe for dev machines, need ops approval for Dedicated.
   - Next: pack as small Go binary, add feature flag, open RFC for Dedicated rollout (INF-482).

2) Small routing policy tweak on the dev proxy (PR #214)
   - Purpose: force low-latency route for requests from local sandbox to avoid cold-path fallback.
   - Outcome: solved flapping in my manual traces, but introduced an edge case where requests > 1024 tokens hit a fallback; pushing a follow-up change.

3) Onboarding checklist iteration
   - Shortened first-run checklist, added one-click steps for starting sandbox (still brittle). Observed faster time-to-first-success for 3 teammates during trial.

Retrospective — what worked:
- Rapid iteration on small infra experiments yields measurable signal quickly (KV warmup + routing tweak).
- Pairing with Evan for PR reviews reduced my cognitive load and kept the PR moving.

Retrospective — what didn't:
- Context switching: navy meetings on Tue/Wed cost ~4h of focused time; led to slower PR turnarounds.
- Lack of test coverage for routing edge-cases meant I regressed on long requests; need better local harness.
- Over-optimization risk: warmed too many prefixes locally (wasted RAM), need a more aggressive LRU policy.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Ops: is pre-warm acceptable for Dedicated pools with tight memory footprints? (blocking for canary)
- Automate selection of top prefixes vs hand-curating — do we use rolling telemetry or static top-keys?
- Should onboarding be a micro-product with dedicated docs + short screencast? I think yes, but needs PM buy-in.

Concrete next actions (short list) — owner = me unless noted:
- [ ] Convert warmup prototype into small Go binary + feature flag (3d)
- [ ] Add unit/system tests for long-request routing edge-case (2d)
- [ ] Draft RFC for Dedicated canary (INF-482) with ops cost estimate (1d)
- [ ] Follow up PR on proxy to handle token-length fallback gracefully (in PR #214 follow-up) (0.5d)
- [ ] Schedule 30m with Maya to sync onboarding doc + screencast plan (this week)

Micro-OKR alignment (personal, Q1) — 3 objectives, measurable outcomes:
- O1 (Faster dev feedback): reduce avg PR review + merge cycle by 30%
  - Key results: <12h avg review time; CI flakiness <5%
- O2 (Safer defaults): introduce a warmed-KV default for dev mode and a guarded canary for Dedicated
  - Key results: first-token latency improvement 15% median on warm path; ops signoff for canary
- O3 (New hire L0): reduce time-to-first-success for new engineers from 2d -> 4h
  - Key results: single-click sandbox start + 5m screencast + checklist validated by 3 new hires

Signals to watch (leading + lagging):
- Telemetry: median first-token cold vs warm, per-region
- PR metrics: review time distribution and number of re-requests for reviewers
- Onboarding success rate (sandbox completions) over 7-day rolling window

Blocks / risks to escalate:
- Memory pressure concern for Dedicated — need ops memory budget number (cc: @ops-oncall in sync)
- No automation to pick top prefixes from telemetry (manual steps hurt reproducibility)

Loose brainstorm (short bullets — half-baked)
- Use a small LRU cache with TTL that is seeded from telemetry on instance create, then continuously refreshed by a low-priority background thread.
- Expose a "warming budget" per deployment tier (hosted/dedicated/private) so teams can opt-in with cost awareness.
- Add a tiny onboarding endpoint that returns a canonical short test prompt which exercises the warmed path for verification.

Notes to self for 1:1 with manager (this week)
- Ask for 8 hours of focus time next Wed to finish the binary + tests.
- Recommend we surface a small internal KPI for onboarding time to motivate PM support.

Random quick log entries (snippets collected during the week)
- "Evan: try warming only top 5 prefixes, memory went down a lot" (11:12am Thu)
- "CI flaked because of network transient; flakiness spike correlated with large artifacts" (Wed evening)
- "Maya liked the screencast; suggested adding checklist task IDs" (Fri pairing)

End-of-week verdict:
- Small wins but still ~50% of planned effort accomplished; need a focused block to finish the warmup binary and tests.
- Recommend moving the warmup RFC to canary path conditional on ops memory budget; will draft and share next Monday.

-- Sofia
